title: model-specific-runtime-optimizations: Llama / Mistral / Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce per-token latency and tail latency for common chat workloads by applying model-specific heuristics and quantization-aware tuning. Several models (Llama-2 family, Mistral series, and Qwen variants) exhibit different attention chunking behavior, KV-cache memory layouts, and GEMM kernel sweet spots when running GQA/MQA quantized weights. This PR introduces targeted runtime adjustments: 1) kernel selection heuristics extended to detect model family and sequence-length distributions and pick tuned GEMM paths for GQA vs MQA; 2) KV cache prefetch & compact-paths for Llama/Mistral that avoid unnecessary copies for short prefix reuse; 3) attention scheduling tweaks for Qwen to reduce workspace fragmentation on A100/RTX-class GPUs; 4) continuous batching improvements that respect model-specific latency SLOs and switch batching windows dynamically; 5) quantization dequant-fusion for hot kernels to reduce memory traffic in MQA paths. The description below contains a concise summary of changes, benchmarks, and reviewer discussion.
commits: feat: add model-family kernel selector; perf: optimize KV cache fast-path for llama/mistral; fix: qwen attention workspace sizing; perf: dynamic batch window + latency SLO hooks; test: add model-specific perf tests and microbenchmarks; docs: runtime tuning notes
changed_files: runtime/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/kernel_selector.h, runtime/gemm_gqa_mqa_kernels.cu, runtime/kv_cache_fastpath.cc, runtime/attention_scheduler.cc, runtime/continuous_batcher.cc, tests/perf/model_specific_bench.cc, docs/runtime/model_tuning.md, scripts/bench/report_gqa_mqa.csv (plus small interface changes in include/runtime.h and CI config)
review_thread:
Michael Chen: Can you explain how kernel selection interacts with the global kernel cache? Is there a risk of cache fragmentation?
Aisha Patel: Kernel selector populates a model-family keyed fastmap. We fall back to global cache for unknown models; added eviction policy to avoid unlimited growth.
Priya Rao: The KV-cache fast-path is great, but please add a unit test for prefix reuse edge-case where prefix grows over multiple requests.
Aisha Patel: Added tests in tests/perf/model_specific_bench.cc and a small regression test under tests/unit/kv_cache_fastpath_test.cc.
Ethan Kim: CI showed a lint failure initially (clang-format) and a flaky nvidia-matmul test. After formatting and adding a retry harness to the test, CI passed. Approving after final bench numbers included.
Michael Chen: Approved.
Merge: squash and merge after minor doc tweak.
ci_checks: Initial CI: failed (clang-format, flaky unit test); Rerun: pass. Matrix: ubuntu-gpu (smoke+perf) - pass; macos - pass; windows - pass; linters - pass; perf/nightly - benchmarks attached to PR. Flaky test introduced a retry wrapper for nv-matmul in tests to stabilize on older drivers.
benchmarks: Local perf (A100, fp16+GQA path): +18% throughput for Llama-2-13B-chat at 512 context, median latency -12% (p50), tail (p99) improved 24% with dynamic batching. Mistral-7B: +13% throughput, p99 -18%. Qwen-7B/14B attention fix reduced workspace OOMs on 32k contexts in internal stress tests; net memory reduction ~7% for long-prefix workloads. KV-cache fast-path reduces token re-encode CPU overhead by ~9% for short prefix reuse patterns.
release_notes:
- Improved runtime kernel selection for GQA/MQA quantized models; better throughput and lower tail latency for Llama/Mistral/Qwen.
- KV-cache fast-path: lower CPU overhead for common prefix reuse patterns.
- Continuous batching now respects per-model latency SLOs and dynamically adjusts batch windows.
- Qwen attention workspace sizing fix reduces OOMs on large-context runs.
notes: Backported the attention workspace sizing fix to release/2026-02 in a follow-up hotfix PR (hotfix/923451). Documentation added under docs/runtime/model_tuning.md with recommended config flags for Dedicated and Private deployments.
